newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CSR sees record Australian sugar crop.
newsitem.headline: CSR sees record Australian sugar crop.

text.p: Australia's biggest sugar refiner, CSR Ltd, said on Friday it was expecting a record Australian sugar crop this year although prices would be lower.
"We're expecting a bigger and another record sugar crop this year, although the sugar price will almost certainly be lower," CSR managing director Geoff Kells told reporters.
Kells was speaking after a Securities Institute of Australia business meeting which followed this week's release of CSR's results for the year ended March 31.

CSR, which is also involved in production of building materials and aluminium, reported a 36 percent drop in annual net profit after abnormal items to A$212.2 million for the year to March 31. The company's sugar business showed a profit fall to A$53.6 million from A$64.7 million in 1995/96.
Kells said the group's refined sugar business was still experiencing intense world competition.
"We are trying to find ways to restructure the (refined sugar) business," Kells said.
However, he said the medium term outlook for Australian raw sugar production was attractive.
"The main increase in raw sugar will be in Asia and Australia is in a good position to supply that market," he said.
CSR would not be seeking to increase its sugar production by offshore acquisitions, Kells said. "The best place to operate our sugar mills is right here (Australia)," he said.
"There is lots of scope to expand raw sugar production, particularly in the (north Queensland) Burdekin and in the Herbert region," he added.
Kells said CSR was continuing to negotiate with local growers to find ways of expanding their production.
"It's much more attractive to do that than to seek opportunities offshore," Kells said.
